test.name: Spec 0023 startup facts: NATS 2.15.1 INFO, listener order, and JetStream under lame duck and a full disk

expected: On nats-server 2.15.1 from the runtime cache, over loopback: the first INFO after start says jetstream true only once JetStream is on, the client listener opens after JetStream starts (also with a 125 MB store of 300 streams), and JetStream is not switched off at run time by a full disk, while SIGUSR2 lame duck stops it with the listener.
actual: (1) the first INFO of every connection made right after start already said jetstream true, and .API.INFO answered account_info_response on that first connection: empty store 179.7 ms after spawn, 127 MB store of 300 streams with 120000 messages 102.3 ms after spawn (JetStream took 85.3 ms to start); no INFO with jetstream true came before JetStream served the API. (2) the client listener opens after JetStream: the log shows Starting JetStream, the stream restores, Took 85.338833ms to start JetStream, and only then Listening for client connections, then Server is ready; the first connect attempt of a 1 ms poll succeeded 102.3 ms after spawn and already got the JetStream API. (3) a full disk (16 MB image, 20 KiB free after 400 publishes of 64 KiB) gave [ERR] Filestore critical write error and JetStream failed to store a msg on the stream, but INFO kept jetstream true and .API.INFO still answered account_info_response without error on two new connections, so NATS did not switch JetStream off; SIGUSR2 (lame duck) logs Entering lame duck mode, Initiating JetStream Shutdown and JetStream Shutdown at once, stops accepting new clients (all 8 attempts in 2 s got connection refused), and an open connection got no .API.INFO reply within 2 s.
steps: extract nats-2.15.1-macos-aarch64 from the xtask runtime cache (sha256 ed0fe39222ec2e317c4d0e1a9cdc16c63ec523d94f9355d24a902a4db2655ffd) into an empty scratch folder and run its nats-server on 127.0.0.1 and a free port with -n golden -js -sd <store>

startup_facts.py: spawn the server and poll connect every 1 ms; each connection reads INFO, sends the exact nats-readiness CONNECT and PING, waits for PONG, then SUB and PUB of .API.INFO; stop at the first account_info_response; keep the -l log (empty store, then a store with 300 file streams of 400 messages of 1 KiB each, 127 MB)

runtime_facts.py lameduck: with a config file (jetstream store_dir, max_file_store 1 GiB) send SIGUSR2 to the ready server, try 8 new connections over 2 s, and ask .API.INFO on a connection opened before
runtime_facts.py fill: mount a 16 MB HFS+ disk image, run the server with the store on it, create a file stream, publish 64 KiB messages until the disk is full, then connect twice and ask .API.INFO
detach the disk image, delete the scratch stores, and check that no scratch nats-server process is left
